title: Correlation between objective and subjective swallowing function in patients with oropharyngeal carcinoma after flap reconstruction surgery
summary:
Background
After surgery in the throat and pharynx area, people may have problems swallowing. These problems are perceived differently in some cases and are not always easy to compare with what is measured during an examination.

Research question
We would like to find out:
How well does what people feel when swallowing correspond to what is visible during an examination?
How do psychological stress or dry mouth affect the sensation of swallowing?

Methodology
Participants complete short questionnaires and their swallowing function is tested in a painless examination. We then compare the personal information with the examination results.
conditions: Oropharyngeal carcinoma after surgical treatment with flap reconstruction

interventions.name: Patients diagnosed with OPSCC who have undergone multimodal therapy with flap reconstruction surgery and have completed therapy at least 3 months ago.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Confirmed OPSCC histology, surgery with flap reconstruction, at least 3 months after completion of therapy, sufficient knowledge of German.
Exclusion criteria:
Severe cognitive impairment, lack of capacity to consent.
